primary_object_card.object_statement: ConstraintBox deterministically governs an evidence-producing attractor-basin challenge whose external Julia, JAX, and PyTorch simulation lanes remain separate from the CB-owned finite SMT checker, run real mathematical operations, retain negative controls, and may be compared only through a typed controller envelope.

source_anchors.quote_or_summary: A sim or proof tool earns status from a bounded executable operation and retained evidence, not package presence or prose.
JAX, Julia, and PyTorch have separate governed runtime roles and package surfaces.
Exact maps, order, named functional, target, and attractor must remain explicit; parity alone does not promote a model claim.
ConstraintBox core, external sim engines, external model audit, and evidence corpus are typed roles that must not be conflated.

primary_object_card.plain_language_definition: This object is a bounded test in which ConstraintBox controls the request, workflow, gates, receipts, retry limits, finite SMT checker, and final claim ceiling while independent Julia, JAX, and PyTorch programs calculate attractor-basin evidence. Those three external engines are test subjects and evidence producers, not parts of the ConstraintBox core. A controller may compare their typed outputs, but no model-written summary can replace their files or decide admission.
weirdness_signature: ConstraintBox governs the run but does not become the external simulation estate
each engine computes independently and cannot read another engine result
wrong and erased controls are first-class results rather than decorative tests
SMT binds finite measured values but cannot certify an unbounded continuous basin
the typed controller envelope compares receipts without becoming a scientific authority

native_terms.ConstraintBox core: The contained deterministic Python controller, formal gates, hooks, loops, receipts, and mini-Lev runtime that govern work.
native_terms.sim engine estate: The separately installed Julia, JAX, PyTorch, numerical, graph, topology, and system-identification libraries exercised as external evidence producers.
native_terms.function receipt: A retained record naming the actual API, input, output, positive control, negative control, boundary, replay, and claim ceiling.
native_terms.typed envelope: A controller-built structure that compares independent engine receipts without silently merging their roles, results, or authority.
native_terms.attractor basin: The set of initial states whose iterates or trajectories approach a named terminal or metastable target under a specified map.

primary_object_card.domain: finite initial-condition grid, explicitly parameterized dynamical map, bounded engine runtimes, deterministic ConstraintBox request and workflow state
primary_object_card.codomain_or_output: independent engine receipts, SMT verdicts, typed comparison envelope, gate decisions, and a literal bounded claim ceiling
allowed_operations: run Julia Attractors and DynamicalSystems basin functions
run JAX x64 vectorized and differentiated basin calculations
run PyTorch autograd, graph, and bounded training calculations
run Z3 and CVC5 finite obligations bound to measured values
run ConstraintBox hooks, loops, retries, gates, and receipt validators
compare only typed controller-selected fields after independent results exist
required_invariants: ConstraintBox core and the external sim engine estate remain separate typed roles
every integrated tool names and executes an actual API rather than reporting import success alone
the Julia, JAX, and PyTorch source programs do not read peer result files, and the CB-owned SMT checker reads only the typed controller bundle
positive, wrong, erased, boundary, and severance outcomes remain distinguishable
all retries are finite and every decision has a deterministic receipt
continuous basin claims stay below proof unless an admitted reachability, interval, or equivalent certificate exists
model audits may stop a run but may not admit or promote it
forbidden_substitutions: LLM verdict or narrative label used as deterministic gate authority
sim engine inventory proxy used as evidence that an API ran
single scalar proxy used as the whole basin partition
cross-engine numerical agreement used as formal proof
ConstraintBox core label substituted for the separate sim engine estate
generated JSON substituted for a real producer receipt
negative_controls: flip the sign of one map parameter so a stability verdict must change
erase one attractor label so the partition-completeness gate must block
scramble one engine runtime identity so provenance validation must block
remove a required external receipt so the typed envelope must park
conflate the sim engine role with ConstraintBox core so the boundary gate must block
sever a producer from its consumer so feedback-closure status must demote
primary_object_card.adapter_policy: Each engine adapter must name the runtime, exact API calls, typed input and output, preserved fields, lost fields, kill control, and bounded claim ceiling. No adapter may promote package presence, agreement, or model prose into proof.
promotion_locks: no scientific or CR promotion from this scratch challenge
no continuous-basin proof without an admitted formal certificate
no whole-estate integration claim from a bounded tool subset
no ConstraintBox self-tuning claim without a live consumer of retained failure records
no final eligible result if any required engine lane is missing or provenance-invalid
primary_object_card.artifact_surface: versioned source files under workers/attractor_basin_v1 and machine-readable receipts under a caller-selected external output directory

lateral_mappings.label: Julia canon lane
lateral_mappings.target: Attractors and DynamicalSystems reference basin partition
loses: global proof outside sampled and certified domain
lateral_mappings.kill_control: remove or alter an attractor definition; the partition and gate verdict must change

lateral_mappings.label: JAX workhorse lane
lateral_mappings.target: x64 JIT and vectorized basin sweep with differentiated stability readouts
lateral_mappings.kill_control: perturb a fixed-point derivative beyond unit magnitude; stability and SMT-linked verdicts must flip

lateral_mappings.label: PyTorch trainable graph lane
lateral_mappings.target: autograd and graph analysis of the same bounded basin problem plus a certified small classifier
lateral_mappings.kill_control: permute training labels or remove graph edges; accuracy or graph invariants must degrade and promotion stays blocked

lateral_mappings.label: SMT finite checker lane
lateral_mappings.target: Z3 and CVC5 checks of finite partition, transition, and stability obligations bound to engine measurements
loses: numerical approximation details outside encoded bounds
preconditions: wrong and erased cases are UNSAT or blocked
lateral_mappings.kill_control: inject a contradictory basin label or erase one state; both solvers and enumeration must reject

lateral_mappings.label: single score summary
lateral_mappings.target: compact human readout of lane completion
lateral_mappings.kill_control: delete a required receipt while retaining the score; the proxy must remain non-authoritative

extended_constraints: source-native terrain and operator test fuel

fixation_breakers: demote agreement to a diagnostic until negative controls and independent replay pass
split any tool bundle whose individual APIs cannot be named and evidenced
replace a stalled grand integration with the smallest failing function receipt

loop_contract.repair_rule: repair the first missing producer, invalid provenance field, or failed kill control before adding another library or claim
loop_contract.stop_condition: all required bounded lanes and controls pass, or a named runtime or certificate dependency remains unavailable after a retained failed receipt

method_contracts.question_is_not_authorization: A question asks for an answer; it is not authorization to implement unless the user explicitly says to do it.
method_contracts.order_check_separate: Any sequence or ordering claim must be checked separately from content correctness, with the order witness named.
method_contracts.baseline_preservation: When debugging runtime behavior, preserve the tuned visible/output baseline and debug the execution path underneath.
method_contracts.falsifier_first: A Popper pass names the target claim, strongest live falsifier, decisive check, and killed/open/survived classification before agreement.
method_contracts.feynman_testability: A Feynman pass names the operation, the observable measured, and the pass/fail condition.
method_contracts.synthesis_refusal: Synthesis must name distinct receipts and explicitly refuse the merge, sequence, or reframe it is not performing.
method_contracts.human_offload: Resolve with tools before asking; ask the human only for private, preference-bound, or unrecoverable information.

evidence_spine.wizard_runtime: Wizard v4.3 object-preservation guard for this current task; it guards the workerized build but does not prove sim success.

source_math_locks.preserves: exact operator maps, precedence, named functional and attractor requirements, and parity claim ceiling
typed separation among ConstraintBox core, external sim engines, model audit, and evidence corpus

evidence_spine.claim_ceiling: scratch diagnostic and function-level integration evidence only; no CR, scientific, continuous-basin proof, whole-estate, or release claim
